title: Two tabs, one document
fullTitle: Two Tabs. One Document. Where Did My Changes Go?

scenes.narration: Tab A saves a new title and the server answers two hundred OK. Then tab B saves, and the old title is back, with no error anywhere.
captions: Tab A saves a new title: 200 OK.
Tab B saves. The old title is back. No error anywhere.

scenes.narration: Rewind. Two independent clients, separate sessions in a local test rather than real browsers, both load the document at version one.
captions: Two independent clients load the same document at version 1.
Separate sessions in a local test, not real browsers.

scenes.narration: A edits the title. B edits only the body, but B's local copy still holds the old title, and saving sends the whole document.
captions: A edits the title. B edits only the body.
B's copy still holds the old title, and saving sends everything.

scenes.narration: The flawed endpoint runs an unconditional update: set the title and body wherever the ID matches. Nothing asks which version B was looking at, so the last writer wins.
captions: The flawed update only asks: does the ID match?
Nothing asks which version B was looking at. Last writer wins.

scenes.narration: The repair sends expectedVersion with the edit. One atomic statement: where the ID and the version both match, replace the content and increment the version. The server then checks how many rows changed. Never a read followed by a write.
captions: One atomic UPDATE: match id AND version, replace, increment.
Check rows changed. Never a separate read, then write.

scenes.narration: Replay. A saves against version one: two hundred, now version two. B also sends version one, matches no row, and receives four oh nine with the current server version.
captions: A saves against version 1: 200, now version 2.
B sends version 1, matches no row: 409 with the current version.

scenes.narration: B's unsaved text is kept, and both versions are shown side by side. A person chooses: take theirs, keep mine, or write a merge. The client never retries by overwriting.
captions: B's unsaved text is kept. Both versions are shown.
A person resolves it. No automatic merge, no overwrite retry.

scenes.narration: Only a version mismatch is a conflict. A locked database returns five oh three, a retryable failure. If two saves race on the same version, exactly one wins. This detects conflicts. It is not real-time collaboration, and not a C R D T.
captions: Only a version mismatch is a 409. A locked database is a 503.
Two racing saves, same version: exactly one is accepted.
Conflict detection, not real-time collaboration, not a CRDT.

scenes.narration: Before saving, check what you are replacing.
captions: Before saving, check what you are replacing.
